title: Counit-compatible shift structure of derived change of rings on a site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the universe of its module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\varphi:R\to S$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Write $K(R)$ for the homotopy category of complexes of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $Q_R:K(R)\to D(R)$ and $Q_S:K(S)\to D(S)$ for the localizations at quasi-isomorphisms, and $s_P:Q_R(P[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(Q_RP)[1]$, $s'_M:Q_S(M[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(Q_SM)[1]$ for their shift isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with $(P[1])^r=P^{r+1}$ and $d_{P[1]}=-d_P$. Let $E:K(R)\to K(S)$ be termwise change of rings $P\mapsto P\otimes_RS$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and let $\theta_P:E(P[1])\to E(P)[1]$ be the identity in every degree (both complexes have $P^{r+1}\otimes_RS$ in degree $r$ and differential $-d_P\otimes1$). Let $F=-\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RS:D(R)\to D(S)$ be the derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], with its derived counit $\varepsilon:F\circ Q_R\to Q_S\circ E$, the natural transformation of the left derived functor of $Q_S\circ E$ [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class]. Then there is a unique family of isomorphisms $\sigma_X:F(X[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(X)[1]$, natural in $X\in D(R)$, such that for every complex $P$ of $R$-modules
$$\varepsilon_P[1]\circ\sigma_{Q_RP}\circ F(s_P)=s'_{E(P)}\circ Q_S(\theta_P)\circ\varepsilon_{P[1]}:\ F(Q_R(P[1]))\to(Q_SE(P))[1],$$
and with this family $(F,\sigma)$ is a triangulated functor [def-weil-triangulated-category]: for every distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1]$ of $D(R)$ the triangle $F(X)\xrightarrow{F(u)}F(Y)\xrightarrow{F(v)}F(Z)\xrightarrow{\sigma_X\circ F(w)}F(X)[1]$ is distinguished in $D(S)$. No flatness of $S$ over $R$ and no boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: The hypothesis E.Additive gives the canonical coherent shift structure on E.mapHomotopyCategory, induced degreewise by identities, and Mathlib proves that this functor preserves the cone triangles. DerivedCategory.Qh is triangulated. Hence B := E.mapHomotopyCategory followed by Q_S is triangulated with its canonical composite shift. These are the cone triangulations of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and [lem-pur-homotopy-category-triangulated], on the module categories of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Definitions 05RR, 05RU and the cone construction in Section 13.11; literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex, Tag 03EK

proof.text: Obtain a DerivedChangeOfRingsCochainModel from [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], retaining the independent source and target localization universes. Its ordinary functor equals E by Functor.ext: h and the model object equalities identify their objects, and hmap and the model map equalities identify their maps after composing equality transports. Thus its K-flat quasi-isomorphism preservation clause applies to E. Let P be the homotopy objects represented by K-flat complexes. Resolve every representative using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; quotient_map_mem_quasiIso_iff gives the homotopy quasi-isomorphism. Lift arrows between such representatives through the full homotopy quotient, apply the K-flat preservation clause, and then localize. Thus B inverts W-arrows between objects of P. The supplied IsLeftDerivedFunctor instance already gives the right Kan universal property of F with counit epsilon; no auxiliary derived pair is chosen.

For every $P$, both $E(P[1])$ and $E(P)[1]$ have degree-$r$ term $P^{r+1}\otimes_R S$ and differential $-d_P\otimes1$. Hence the degreewise identities give the natural isomorphism $\theta_P$. For an integer shift $n$, replace $1$ by $n$ and the minus sign by $(-1)^n$; composition of these identities gives the zero and addition coherence identities. Together with the localization shift structure, this gives the coherent shift comparison of $B=Q_S\circ E$, whose degree-one component is $b_P=s'_{E(P)}\circ Q_S(\theta_P):B(P[1])\to B(P)[1]$.

source.place: Tag 05SU(2), together with the complex-shift definition in Section 13.11 and the termwise tensor construction in sites-modules.tex Tag 03EK

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-right-kan-extension-coherent-shift] to B, Q_R, the supplied F and epsilon, using the right Kan property contained in the given IsLeftDerivedFunctor instance. It supplies a coherent CommShift structure on F and NatTrans.CommShift epsilon. Evaluate NatTrans.shift_app_comm at 1 and P, expand the two composite CommShift components, and reassociate. This is precisely the displayed counit equation.

source.place: Tag 05SU(2) and Proposition 05SE, LF part; generic universal-property formulation

proof.text: Postcomposition with the target shift H = [1] preserves the right Kan property: the functor RightExtension.postcompose₂ Q_R B H is an equivalence, obtained from the equivalence given by whiskering with H and the associator natural isomorphism. Transport the terminal right-extension object along this equivalence. The resulting counit gamma for F followed by H is associator.inv followed by whiskerRight epsilon H. If tau and sigma satisfy the counit equation, cancel the common isomorphism F(s_P) to obtain equality after postcomposition with H(epsilon_P). These are the components of whiskerLeft Q_R tau.hom followed by gamma and of the same expression with sigma.hom. Right Kan hom_ext identifies tau.hom and sigma.hom, and Iso.ext identifies the isomorphisms. This argument imposes no coherence or triangle-preservation hypothesis on tau.

By [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated], W has the two fraction calculi, two-out-of-three and the saturated triangulated multiplicative-system property. Apply [lem-pur-resolving-class-essential-constancy] to B and the class P from step 2 to obtain essential constancy at every homotopy object. Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-kan-source-triangles] with the coherent shift on F from step 4 and its compatible counit: Q_R followed by F preserves distinguished source triangles. The localization representation [lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6] writes every distinguished derived triangle as an isomorphic image of a distinguished homotopy triangle. Map that representing isomorphism by F.mapTriangle and compose with mapTriangleCompIso to deduce F.IsTriangulated with this same shift comparison. Its standard Mathlib instance gives F.Additive. Finally F.map_distinguished is exactly the displayed Triangle.mk conclusion.

reviewed.note:
mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q105-9693d743d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all six steps in full, the statements of all 12 cited nodes, unit sk-rem-rest (a remark with no steps, so no route), the reviewed parent lem-weil-pbc-scalar-extension-unit-triangles, Stacks derived.tex 05SU (l.4657) and 05SE (l.4895), sites-cohomology.tex 06YY (l.3585), and the main-20261015 prop-weil-pbc-levelwise-truncations proof Step 1. The statement is true, and its coefficient categories match 06YY: R- and S-module sheaves on a small site, unbounded, with no flatness or boundedness assumed. The displayed equation is exactly the condition that the counit ε commutes with shifts. Edge cases checked: S=0, R=S, P=0, unbounded P. The delivery has no new nodes. I searched for duplicates (counit/shift, derived change of rings, 05SU) and found none.

Steps 1-5 are correct as written. Step 1: the termwise tensor preserves the cone matrix and homotopies. Step 2: both hypotheses of lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class hold, from lem-pc-kflat-resolution and clause (1) of lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings. Step 3: θ is the identity in every degree. Step 4: lem-pur-right-kan-extension-coherent-shift applies to B=Q_S∘E, and expanding its conclusion gives the displayed equation. Step 5: uniqueness follows from injectivity of the Kan correspondence for H=[-1]F[1].

One fault, C3/C4, in step 6. The step took exactness from lem-pur-left-derived-exact-when-defined, whose statement never says which shift comparison it uses. It then identified that comparison with the step-4 σ by step 5's uniqueness. But step 5 only applies to comparisons already known to satisfy the counit equation, and that fact is in the cited node's proof, not its statement. The point matters: with -σ the image triangles are not distinguished. I rewrote step 6 using statements only. lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated and lem-pur-resolving-class-essential-constancy give essential constancy. lem-pur-left-derived-kan-source-triangles, applied with σ from step 4, makes images of homotopy-category triangles distinguished. lem-pur-localization-triangles-05r6 (Mathlib leaf) and TR1 extend this to every triangle, with the third square written out from naturality of σ. proof_deps and tool_uses are updated: lem-pur-left-derived-exact-when-defined is dropped, kan-source-triangles and resolving-class-essential-constancy are added. I checked that the new citations create no cycle. All other declared tool_uses are accepted as generic black boxes, since the remark unit has no route. The corrected file is at fixes/dag/nodes/sec-smooth-base-change/lem-sbc-derived-scalar-extension-counit-shift.json; details are in review.md.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
